blocks.content: There shall be a Parliament for the Union which shall consist of the President and two Houses to be known respectively as the Council of States and the House of the People.

rows: People of India as a whole
Permanent body (1/3rd members retire every 2 years)

items: The President is an integral part of Parliament under Article 79, even though they do not sit or participate in discussions in either House.
A Bill passed by both Houses cannot become an Act without the assent of the President.
Distinguish clearly between the Council of States (Rajya Sabha / Upper House) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha / Lower House).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 79 explicitly establishes the Constitution of Parliament for the Union of India.
The Indian Parliament consists of three integral parts: the President, the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
Though the President is not a member of either House of Parliament, they are an indispensable part of the parliamentary system.
Rajya Sabha represents the States and Union Territories, while Lok Sabha represents the people of India as a whole.
